# TTS.Rocks

Generate and download speech for videos, tutorials and narration in a browser.

For PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOCX or ODT, choose "Upload file" (#uploadDocument) or set files on #documentFile, review the extracted text, choose voices and click "Generate Episode". Files are read locally. Document mode supports 100,000 characters and uses current studio settings. In-page functions: ttsRocks.documents.import(file), useText(text, name), generate(), status(), cancel(), download("wav"), download("vtt"). Keep the tab open; completed sections can be resumed with unchanged text and settings. See the automation guide for Playwright downloads. The CLI helper handles short requests and batches; documents use browser controls/functions.

- [Automation guide](https://tts.rocks/automation.md): browser controls, public window.ttsRocks functions, download handling, options and batch generation.
- [Website](https://tts.rocks/): open "Use with an AI assistant" to copy Markdown instructions or the selected voice settings.
- [CLI helper](https://tts.rocks/tts-rocks.mjs): Node.js and Playwright helper that uses the website and saves WAV, VTT and JSON files.

Local models download into the browser cache. No native TTS engine or Python installation is required. This is not a server-side HTTP synthesis endpoint; a JavaScript-capable browser is necessary. Direct functions and the CLI support Kokoro, Kitten 0.8, Supertonic and Chatterbox. Other engines use the labelled studio controls. Browser Native cannot export audio.

Inside the page: await ttsRocks.ready(); await ttsRocks.listVoices({engine: "kokoro"}); const result = await ttsRocks.generate({text: "Welcome.", voice: "af_aoede"}); ttsRocks.download(result.id, "narration.wav"). Save downloads before closing the browser or generating the next recording. See the guide for Playwright saveAs and CLI examples.
